title: Shelter beds for the homeless and how people move on to longer-term housing
asked: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked how many homeless shelter beds are run by the Government and by charitable organisations, what measures help residents move to longer-term housing, and what the success rate of those transitions is for homeless youths and young adults under 35.
response: Mr Eric Chua said there are seven MSF-funded Transitional Shelters and 20 Safe Sound Sleeping Places run by charitable organisations or volunteer groups, with 730 and 160 bed spaces respectively. Transitional Shelters provide onsite social work intervention and link residents to community partners and volunteers, and youths and young adults aged 35 may exit to stable long-term accommodation such as reconciling with family, open market rental or the HDB Public Rental Scheme. Based on recent data, the average length of stay for youths and young adults in Transitional Shelters was seven months, against 10 months for individuals in Transitional Shelters. He pointed the Member to the 2025 MSF Street Count report published on 9 January 2026.

key_points.point: There are seven MSF-funded Transitional Shelters and 20 Safe Sound Sleeping Places run by charitable organisations or volunteer groups.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: there are currently seven Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)-funded Transitional Shelters and 20 Safe Sound Sleeping Places (S3Ps) run by charitable organisations or volunteer groups

key_points.point: Total bed spaces are 730 in Transitional Shelters and 160 in S3Ps.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: The total bed spaces are 730 and 160 respectively.

key_points.point: Transitional Shelters provide onsite social work intervention and link residents to community partners and volunteers for social support.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: Transitional Shelters provide onsite social work intervention to residents to help them address underlying issues and work towards stable long-term accommodation options.

key_points.point: Youths and young adults aged 35 may exit to stable long-term accommodation, including reconciling with family, open market rental or the HDB Public Rental Scheme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: Some reconcile with their families, while others move to open market rental, or to the Housing and Development Board (HDB) Public Rental Scheme.

key_points.point: Average length of stay for youths and young adults in Transitional Shelters was seven months, compared with 10 months for individuals in Transitional Shelters.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: the average length of stay for youths and young adults in Transitional Shelters was seven months, compared to 10 months for individuals in Transitional Shelters

key_points.point: The 2025 MSF Street Count report was published on 9 January 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: I will also invite the Member to refer to the 2025 MSF Street Count report, published recently on 9 January 2026

key_points.point: SSO officers accompany PEERS Network community partners on weekly night walks.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: our Social Service Office (SSO) officers do accompany our Partners Engaging and Empowering Rough Sleepers (PEERS) Network community partners on a weekly basis, whenever they conduct the night walks

key_points.point: MSF works with community partners to maintain sufficient surge capacity for shelter beds.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: we work very closely with our community partners to make sure that there is sufficient surge capacity

key_points.point: In the 2025 nationwide street count, about 30 of 496 rough sleepers were young people, up from about 16 of 530 in 2022.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: Last year, where we did our nationwide street count again in 2025, of the 496 rough sleepers, we had about 30.

key_points.point: The predominant profile of the rough sleeper in Singapore is male, middle-aged to older Chinese individuals, many still in employment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: the predominant profile of the rough sleeper in Singapore is still male, middle-aged to older Chinese individuals

key_points.point: Half of rough sleepers have homes to return to.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: Half of them do have homes to go back to

left_open: A success rate for transitions from shelters into longer-term housing.
Employment opportunities, skills training and mental health services for homeless youth and young adults.
supplementary: Outreach to rough sleepers, how shelter bed capacity is assessed and expanded, and support beyond housing for homeless youth.
